module Knowledge
  class EmbeddingJob
    def call(document_id:, tenant_id:, version:, provider:)
      snapshot = Document.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
      return :discarded unless snapshot

      vector = provider.call(snapshot.body)
      Document.transaction do
        current = Document.lock.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
        current ||= snapshot

        Embedding.upsert({ document_id: current.id, tenant_id: tenant_id, revision: current.revision,
                           version: version, vector: JSON.generate(vector) }, unique_by: %i[document_id version])
      end
      :stored
    end
  end
end
--- packs/knowledge/app/services/knowledge/publish_delivery.rb
# frozen_string_literal: true

module Knowledge
  class PublishDelivery
    def call(delivery_id:, store:)
      delivery = Delivery.find(delivery_id)
      payload = JSON.parse(delivery.payload)
      begin
        store.publish(id: delivery.event_id, type: 'DocumentPublished', data: payload)
      rescue store.duplicate_error
        existing = store.read(delivery.event_id)
        raise 'conflicting event' unless existing == { type: 'DocumentPublished', data: payload }
      end
      delivery.update!(delivered: true)
      :delivered
    end
  end
end

module Knowledge
  class RebuildSearch
    def call(index:, after_backfill: -> {})
      candidate = index.create_candidate
      index.replace(candidate, documents)
      after_backfill.call
      Document.transaction do
        index.replace(candidate, documents)
        raise 'candidate validation failed' unless index.valid?(candidate, documents)

        index.activate(candidate)
      end
      candidate
    end

    private

    def documents
      Document.where(published: true).order(:id).map do |document|
        document.attributes.slice('id', 'tenant_id', 'body', 'revision')
      end
    end
  end

steps.message: The current job has two defects: it falls back to the original snapshot when the authoritative row disappears/changes, and it writes that stale snapshot’s revision. I’ll replace that fallback with an exact revision/tenant/publication check inside a transaction, and guard the unique `(document_id, version)` write so an embedding carrying a newer revision cannot be replaced. Provider invocation will remain before this transaction. I’ll also verify behavior with focused tests for withdrawal, revision changes, tenant changes, provider failures, and version coexistence.

module Knowledge
  class EmbeddingJob
    def call(document_id:, tenant_id:, version:, provider:)
      snapshot = Document.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
      return :discarded unless snapshot

      # Provider calls can be slow (and can call back into the application), so they
      # must not hold a database transaction open.
      vector = provider.call(snapshot.body)

      Document.transaction do
        current = Document.lock.find_by(id: document_id)
        unless current && current.tenant_id == tenant_id && current.published? &&
               current.revision == snapshot.revision
          raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
        end

        embedding = Embedding.lock.find_by(document_id: document_id, version: version)
        if embedding && (embedding.tenant_id != tenant_id || embedding.revision > snapshot.revision)
          raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
        end

        attributes = {
          document_id: document_id,
          tenant_id: tenant_id,
          revision: snapshot.revision,
          version: version,
          vector: JSON.generate(vector)
        }

        if embedding
          embedding.update!(attributes)
        else
          Embedding.create!(attributes)
        end
      end

      # Rollback is used above as a simple way to leave the transaction without
      # writing. The transaction's return value distinguishes that case from a
      # successful write without exposing a new public API.
      :stored
    rescue ActiveRecord::Rollback
      :discarded
    end
  end
end

I’m correcting this to return an explicit transaction result, with no exception handling around the provider, then I’ll exercise the stale and error paths.

The Rails transaction returns :discarded without a raise, so I should make sure there's a separate branch for that. I'll also remove the rescue since it doesn't seem to catch the errors effectively when they come from the provider.

require_relative 'test_helper'

class EmbeddingJobTest < BenchmarkTest
  def test_revision_change_during_provider_is_discarded
    doc = document
    result = job.call(document_id: doc.id, tenant_id: 'a', version: 'v1', provider: lambda { |_body|
      doc.update!(revision: 2)
      [1]
    })
    assert_equal :discarded, result
    assert_empty Knowledge::Embedding.all
  end

  def test_withdrawal_and_tenant_change_during_provider_are_discarded
    doc = document
    result = job.call(document_id: doc.id, tenant_id: 'a', version: 'v1', provider: lambda { |_body|
      doc.update!(published: false)
      [1]
    })
    assert_equal :discarded, result
    assert_empty Knowledge::Embedding.all

    doc.update!(published: true)
    result = job.call(document_id: doc.id, tenant_id: 'a', version: 'v2', provider: lambda { |_body|
      doc.update!(tenant_id: 'b')
      [2]
    })
    assert_equal :discarded, result
    assert_empty Knowledge::Embedding.all
  end

  def test_provider_error_does_not_write
    doc = document
    error = assert_raises(RuntimeError) do
      job.call(document_id: doc.id, tenant_id: 'a', version: 'v1', provider: ->(_body) { raise 'failed' })
    end
    assert_equal 'failed', error.message
    assert_empty Knowledge::Embedding.all
  end

  def test_versions_coexist_and_newer_revision_is_not_overwritten
    doc = document
    assert_equal :stored, job.call(document_id: doc.id, tenant_id: 'a', version: 'v1', provider: ->(_body) { [1] })
    doc.update!(revision: 2)
    assert_equal :stored, job.call(document_id: doc.id, tenant_id: 'a', version: 'v2', provider: ->(_body) { [2] })
    assert_equal %w[v1 v2], Knowledge::Embedding.order(:version).pluck(:version)

    doc.update!(revision: 1)
    result = job.call(document_id: doc.id, tenant_id: 'a', version: 'v2', provider: ->(_body) { [99] })
    assert_equal :discarded, result
    assert_equal '[2]', Knowledge::Embedding.find_by!(version: 'v2').vector
  end

  private

  def job
    Knowledge::EmbeddingJob.new
  end
end
